sections.heading: Core Gameplay Mechanics
sections.body:
Contortionist Memory Match's core gameplay revolves around the concept of sliding tiles to reassemble a picture. Players can move the tiles by touching or clicking on them, which will swap the positions of the two tiles. The game's simplicity lies in its intuitive controls, making it easy for players to pick up and play. As players progress through the levels, the game introduces new challenges, such as time limits, obstacles, and power-ups, which add an extra layer of depth to the gameplay experience.

The game's tile-swapping mechanism is the key to solving puzzles, and players must use strategy and problem-solving skills to move the tiles to their correct positions. The game's grid system allows players to move tiles horizontally and vertically, but not diagonally, which adds an extra layer of complexity to the gameplay experience. As players progress through the levels, the game introduces new tile types, such as locked tiles, which can only be moved by solving a specific sequence of tiles.

Players can also use special power-ups, such as the 'shuffle' power-up, which randomizes the tile positions, and the 'lock' power-up, which locks a specific tile in place. These power-ups can be used strategically to help players solve puzzles or to gain an advantage over their opponents. With its intuitive controls and engaging gameplay, Contortionist Memory Match's core gameplay mechanics make it an excellent choice for players of all ages and skill levels.

The game's level design is another key aspect of its core gameplay mechanics. Each level presents a unique puzzle, with a specific set of tiles and objectives. Players must use their problem-solving skills to move the tiles to their correct positions and complete the puzzle. The game's level design is carefully crafted to introduce new challenges and obstacles, which adds an extra layer of complexity to the gameplay experience.
